description: Golden test dataset for TenderSync RAG evaluation - 100 complex RFP/contract queries

difficulties.hard: Requires multi-hop reasoning or complex table understanding

samples.query: What ISO certifications are required for bid submission?
samples.ground_truth: The RFP requires ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management), ISO 27001:2013 (Information Security), and ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management) certifications. All three must be current and valid through the contract period.
relevant_chunks: Section 4.2 Mandatory Certifications: Bidders must hold current certifications for ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management Systems), ISO 27001:2013 (Information Security Management Systems), and ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management Systems). All certifications must remain valid through the proposed contract period of [start date] to [end date].

samples.query: What is the total contract value and payment schedule?
samples.ground_truth: The total contract value is AUD 2,500,000 (Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Australian Dollars). Payment schedule: 20% upon contract signing, 30% at Month 6 milestone, 30% at Month 12 milestone, and 20% upon final deliverables acceptance.
relevant_chunks: Section 3.1 Contract Value: The total contract value is AUD 2,500,000 (Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Australian Dollars) exclusive of GST.

Section 3.2 Payment Schedule: Payments will be made as follows: (a) 20% upon execution of the Contract, (b) 30% upon achievement of Month 6 milestones, (c) 30% upon achievement of Month 12 milestones, and (d) 20% upon acceptance of final deliverables and project closure.

samples.query: When is the submission deadline and are late submissions accepted?
samples.ground_truth: The submission deadline is 5:00 PM AEST on Friday, 15 March 2026. Late submissions will NOT be accepted under any circumstances. The RFP explicitly states: 'Any tender submitted after the closing date and time will be deemed non-responsive and will not be evaluated.'
relevant_chunks: Section 2.1 Submission Deadline: All completed tender submissions must be received no later than 5:00 PM Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) on Friday, 15 March 2026.

Section 2.3 Late Submissions: Any tender submitted after the closing date and time will be deemed non-responsive and will not be evaluated. No extensions will be granted except in exceptional circumstances at the sole discretion of the Agency.

samples.query: What are the mandatory insurance requirements?
samples.ground_truth: Bidders must maintain: (1) Public Liability Insurance of minimum AUD 10,000,000, (2) Professional Indemnity Insurance of minimum AUD 5,000,000, (3) Workers Compensation Insurance as required by state legislation, and (4) Cyber Liability Insurance of minimum AUD 2,000,000. All policies must name the Agency as an additional insured.
relevant_chunks: Section 5.1 Insurance Requirements: The Supplier shall maintain, at its own expense, the following minimum insurance coverage throughout the Contract period: (a) Public Liability Insurance: AUD 10,000,000 per occurrence; (b) Professional Indemnity Insurance: AUD 5,000,000 per claim; (c) Workers Compensation: As required by applicable state/territory legislation; (d) Cyber Liability Insurance: AUD 2,000,000 per occurrence. The Agency shall be named as an additional insured on all policies.

samples.query: What is the required experience for the project team leader?
samples.ground_truth: The Project Team Leader must have: (1) minimum 10 years of relevant experience in delivery of similar government IT projects, (2) at least 3 years of experience managing projects with budget exceeding AUD 1,000,000, (3) PMP or PRINCE2 certification preferred, and (4) demonstrated experience with Agile delivery frameworks in government context.
relevant_chunks: Section 6.3 Project Team Leader Requirements: The nominated Project Team Leader must possess: (a) a minimum of ten (10) years of relevant industry experience; (b) at least three (3) years of experience managing projects with total budget exceeding AUD 1,000,000; (c) Project Management Professional (PMP) or PRINCE2 Practitioner certification (preferred but not mandatory); and (d) demonstrated experience in delivering government IT projects using Agile methodologies.

samples.query: What ABN requirements must be met?
samples.ground_truth: The supplier must hold a valid Australian Business Number (ABN) issued by the Australian Business Register. The ABN must be active and not suspended or cancelled. Additionally, if the supplier is a corporation, the ACN (Australian Company Number) must be provided. The supplier must also be registered for GST if the contract value exceeds AUD 10,000.
relevant_chunks: Section 1.4 Legal Eligibility: (a) The Supplier must hold a current and valid Australian Business Number (ABN) registered with the Australian Business Register. (b) If the Supplier is a corporation, the Australian Company Number (ACN) must be provided. (c) Suppliers must be registered for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if the proposed contract value exceeds AUD 10,000.

samples.query: What is the expected duration of the contract?
samples.ground_truth: The contract is for an initial period of 24 months commencing on 1 July 2026, with two optional extension periods of 12 months each, subject to satisfactory performance review. The total potential contract duration is 48 months (4 years).
relevant_chunks: Section 3.3 Contract Period: The initial Contract Period shall be twenty-four (24) months commencing on 1 July 2026. The Agency may, at its discretion, extend the Contract for up to two (2) further periods of twelve (12) months each, subject to satisfactory performance review. The maximum potential Contract Period is forty-eight (48) months.

samples.query: What are the penalties for non-performance?
samples.ground_truth: The contract includes liquidated damages of 0.5% of the monthly fee for each week of delay, capped at 10% of the total contract value. Additionally, failure to meet any critical milestone may result in termination for cause, with 30 days notice. The supplier must also reimburse the agency for any costs incurred due to the supplier's failure to perform.
relevant_chunks: Section 7.2 Liquidated Damages: In the event of delay in delivery of Services, the Supplier shall pay liquidated damages at the rate of 0.5% of the monthly service fee for each week of delay, up to a maximum of 10% of the total Contract Value.

Section 7.3 Termination for Cause: The Agency may terminate this Contract for cause if the Supplier fails to meet any Critical Milestone, upon thirty (30) days written notice. The Supplier shall reimburse the Agency for all costs incurred as a result of the Supplier's failure to perform.

samples.query: What security clearance levels are required for staff?
samples.ground_truth: All staff working on this project must hold or be eligible for: (1) Baseline confidentiality clearance for all team members, (2) NV1 (Negative Vetting 1) clearance for system administrators and database administrators, and (3) NV2 (Negative Vetting 2) clearance for the Project Team Leader and security architect. Cleared staff must be exclusively employed by the supplier (no subcontractors without prior approval).
relevant_chunks: Section 8.2 Security Clearances: All personnel working on this Contract shall hold or be eligible for the following minimum security clearances: (a) Baseline: All team members; (b) NV1 (Negative Vetting Level 1): System Administrators, Database Administrators, and Network Engineers; (c) NV2 (Negative Vetting Level 2): Project Team Leader and Security Architect. All personnel must be directly employed by the Supplier; subcontractors require prior written approval.

samples.query: What is the warranty period for deliverables?
samples.ground_truth: All deliverables are warranted for a period of 12 months from the date of acceptance. During the warranty period, the supplier must fix any defects at no additional cost. The warranty covers functionality defects but excludes issues caused by changes to the operating environment or misuse.
relevant_chunks: Section 9.4 Warranty: The Supplier warrants all Deliverables for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of acceptance ('Warranty Period'). During the Warranty Period, the Supplier shall, at its own cost, rectify any defects in the Deliverables. This warranty does not cover issues arising from: (a) changes to the operating environment; (b) misuse or improper handling; or (c) modifications not authorized by the Supplier.

_comment: The full dataset contains 100 samples. This is a representative sample of 10 across all categories and difficulties. The complete dataset includes complex multi-table financial schedules, cross-referenced clauses, and Australian-specific tender requirements.
